1:
Let $d$ be your first distance from the wall and $h_1$ your friend's first height: $h_1=d\tan62^\circ$. At distance $2d$: $h_2=2d\tan46^\circ$ and $h_2=h_1+8$.
\[2d\tan46^\circ=d\tan62^\circ+8\ \Rightarrow\ d=\frac{8}{2\tan46^\circ-\tan62^\circ}\approx42.03\ \text{ft}.\]
So $h_2=2d\tan46^\circ\approx\boxed{87.0\ \text{ft}}$ (it was $\approx79.0$ ft at the first measurement).
2:
Center the mud circle at the origin (radius 20). The westernmost point is $(-20,0)$, so the cat starts at $(-20,-30)$. It heads toward $(20+5,\,0+11)=(25,11)$, direction $\langle45,41\rangle$: $(x,y)=(-20+45s,\,-30+41s)$.

It reaches $y=0$ (due east of the center) at $s=\frac{30}{41}$, the point $(12.927,0)$. It entered the mud when $(-20+45s)^2+(-30+41s)^2=400$:
\[3706s^2-4260s+900=0\Rightarrow s\approx0.2731,\ \text{entry}\approx(-7.446,\,-18.562).\]
Mud walked on the first leg: distance from $(-7.446,-18.562)$ to $(12.927,0)$ $\approx27.56$ m. Then east from $(12.927,0)$ to the edge $(20,0)$: $7.07$ m.

Time in the mud: $\dfrac{27.56+7.07}{1.3}\approx\boxed{26.6\ \text{s}}$.
3:
Let $t$ be years after 2000. Bullm: $B(t)=7000\cdot2^{(t-5)/17}$, so $B(11)=7000\cdot2^{6/17}\approx8940.1$.

Aarb: $A(t)=5000\,b^t$ with $A(11)=2B(11)\approx17880.3$, so $b=(3.5761)^{1/11}\approx1.12282$.

Set $A(t)=40000$: $b^t=8\Rightarrow t=\dfrac{\ln8}{\ln b}\approx\boxed{17.95\ \text{years after 2000}}$.
4:
Let $t$ be hours after midnight yesterday. Max 6 cm at $t=11$, min 5 cm at $t=20$: half-period 9 h, period 18 h, midline 5.5, amplitude 0.5:
\[L(t)=5.5+0.5\cos\!\Big(\frac{2\pi}{18}(t-11)\Big).\]
$5.2<L<5.6\iff -0.6<\cos\!\big(\frac{\pi}{9}(t-11)\big)<0.2$. Solving over $0\le t\le24$ gives
\[(4.66,\,7.08),\ (14.92,\,17.34),\ (22.66,\,24],\]
so the whiskers were in that range for about $2.42+2.42+1.34\approx\boxed{6.18\ \text{hours}}$.
5:
\textbf{(a)} Jerry: $(-5,5)\to(10,0)$ in 5 s: $x_J=-5+3t,\ y_J=5-t$.

\textbf{(b)} Tom: $(0,9)\to(4,-3)$ in 4 s: $x_T=t,\ y_T=9-3t$.

\textbf{(c)} Squared distance:
\[D(t)=(x_J-x_T)^2+(y_J-y_T)^2=(2t-5)^2+(2t-4)^2=8t^2-36t+41,\]
smallest at $t=\frac{36}{16}=\boxed{2.25\ \text{s}}$ (distance $\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\approx0.71$ m).
6:
At 4 km/h: north 1 km takes $\frac14$ h, east 2 km takes $\frac12$ h, south 3 km takes $\frac34$ h. With the start at the origin:
\begin{itemize}
\item $0\le t\le0.25$: $(0,4t)$.
\item $0.25\le t\le0.75$: $(4t-1,\,1)$.
\item $0.75\le t\le1.5$: $(2,\,1-4(t-0.75))=(2,\,4-4t)$.
\end{itemize}
\[d(t)=\begin{cases}4t, & 0\le t\le0.25\\ \sqrt{(4t-1)^2+1}, & 0.25<t\le0.75\\ \sqrt{4+(4-4t)^2}, & 0.75<t\le1.5\end{cases}\quad\text{(km)}\]
7:
\textbf{(a)} $f(g(x))=(3x-1)+2|3x-4|$.

If $x\ge\frac43$: $3x-1+6x-8=-4x\Rightarrow x=\frac9{13}$, but $\frac9{13}<\frac43$: rejected.

If $x<\frac43$: $3x-1-6x+8=-4x\Rightarrow -3x+7=-4x\Rightarrow x=-7$ \checkmark.

Solution: \boxed{x=-7}.

\textbf{(b)} $h(x)=g(\sqrt x)+x+1=3\sqrt x-1+x+1=x+3\sqrt x$ for $x\ge0$. Set $y=x+3\sqrt x$ and $u=\sqrt x\ge0$: $u^2+3u-y=0$, so $u=\frac{-3+\sqrt{9+4y}}{2}$. Hence
\[h^{-1}(x)=\Big(\frac{-3+\sqrt{9+4x}}{2}\Big)^2,\quad x\ge0.\]
